sections.topic: Transport by thermal motion; role of medium
claims: Diffusion involves thermally driven motion of atoms or molecules
Rates depend on both moving species and medium
examples: Incense, ink spreading, rusting; hot/cold ink activity
sections.disposition: Use as motivation; qualify ink activity because convection and density flows can dominate visible spreading. Do not infer universal gas>liquid>solid rate ordering for arbitrary species/conditions.

claims: Graham, Fick, Roberts-Austen, Arrhenius, self-diffusion, Brownian motion and random-motion theory
sections.disposition: Optional short historical sidebar only after external primary/history verification. Caption dates/names are unreliable; L1 associates Fick with 1848 while L3 says 1855. Do not repeat unverified awards, dates, or naming trivia.

examples: Peritectic product layer and slowing growth
sections.disposition: Give mechanisms and transport paths without declaring every process universally diffusion-rate-controlled. Distinguish thermodynamic driving force from kinetic rate limitation. Avoid inferring specific phase-diagram coordinates from unseen slides.
Provide concise calculus reference with precise one-sided limits, finite partitions for piecewise continuity, and derivative domains. Absolute value is nonnegative, not strictly positive.

sections.correction: For y=2x², y'=4x, so slope at x=1 is 4 and tangent y=4x−2. Caption says slope8 and tangent4x+1. A zero derivative is necessary for an interior differentiable local extremum, not sufficient; x³ at zero is a counterexample. Second derivative zero is inconclusive.

examples: Integration by parts e^x sin x and log x
Reflection symmetry gives integral sin⁴/(sin⁴+cos⁴) over [0,pi/2] = pi/4
sections.disposition: Preserve the calculus mechanisms that will be reused. Use ln|x| and absolute-value ratios on appropriate domains; integration constants can be fixed by initial data even for indefinite antiderivatives.

sections.topic: Fick first law and its limitations
claims: Vector gradient relation for isotropic diffusion
Concentration-dependent D, anisotropy, reactions, fields and fast paths
sections.correction: The local first law is a constitutive relation usable in transient as well as steady diffusion. D(c) does not require changing the first-law form; it changes the resulting PDE. Reactions enter the balance source term. Directional/chemical coupling must be stated separately.

sections.topic: Control-volume balance and Fick second law
claims: Flux times area and concentration rate times volume have matching amount/time units
partial_t c=div(D grad c); constant D gives D Laplacian c
sections.disposition: Derive explicitly with correct signs and volume. The intentionally incomplete equation at ~638–759s is an exercise, not an unresolved source error. For spatially varying but concentration-independent D the equation remains linear, so do not call every nonconstant-D case nonlinear.

claims: r²=x²+y², x=r cos theta, y=r sin theta
Gradient and divergence in cylindrical coordinates
sections.disposition: Add a developed radial-shell balance or coordinate derivation. Correct radial equation is partial_t c=(1/r) partial_r(rD partial_r c); spherical radial equation uses r². Avoid calling radial transport axial. Basis derivatives matter when deriving divergence.

claims: Cubic isotropy; uniaxial D_perp sin²theta+D_parallel cos²theta
sections.correction: The complete tensor in an arbitrary laboratory frame needs orientation as well as principal values. Orthorhombic, monoclinic and triclinic independent-component counts differ; do not assert three numbers fully specify every arbitrary-frame tensor. Flux need not be parallel to the concentration gradient; distinguish projected directional coefficient from vector flux.

sections.disposition: Retain conceptual questions but qualify diffusion involvement versus rate control. Nonsteady behavior means at least some concentration changes, not that every point necessarily changes. Derivative is 3x(x²−3)cos x+9(x²−1)sin x.

Clarify that m=-4 makes divergence vanish at that point only. No constant m gives a source-free steady field everywhere for the displayed polynomial. Treat coordinates/coefficients as dimensionally scaled or supply units.

Define s with inverse-time units and a convergence half-plane; transform time while leaving space as a parameter. Do not imply transforms make arbitrary equations easier or that all kernels share a domain.

examples: L[sin(at)]=a/(s²+a²) via two integrations by parts
sections.disposition: Show convergence conditions and the improper-limit step, not exp(−infinity) without its coefficient/sign condition.
State sufficient regularity/exponential-order assumptions and boundary decay. Derive the initial terms by integration by parts.
Reproduce both initial conditions and differential residual.

sections.topic: Forced ODE example and partial fractions
sections.correction: Correct result is y=2cos t+(5/3)sin t−(1/3)sin2t. F=2s/(s²+1)+(5/3)/(s²+1)−(2/3)/(s²+4); inverse last term divides its numerator by frequency2. Caption correction still says −2/3 sin2t, which fails initial derivative and forcing.

examples: G(x)=integral_0^1 (u^x−1)/ln u du; G'=1/(x+1), G0=0, G3=ln4
sections.disposition: State x>−1 and domination on compact subintervals of that domain; endpoint singularity at u=1 is removable. Distinguish this auxiliary x from physical position when teaching.

claims: Initial spatial distribution appears as inhomogeneous term
sections.disposition: The lecturer corrects the missing /D around 1011s. Preserve the corrected equation; a sufficient dominated-convergence condition justifies moving x derivatives through the improper integral. General solution for arbitrary nonzero initial condition needs a particular solution, not only exponential homogeneous modes.

sections.correction: Partial fractions are 3/s+(5s−4)/(s²+4), so inverse is 3+5cos2t−2sin2t. Caption mutates coefficients (−3,−3/2). Verify original slide before quoting its numerical claim.

sections.disposition: It is neither continuous nor piecewise continuous under the finite-one-sided-limit definition, because the right limit at1 diverges; the word jump alone understates the defect.

sections.topic: Completing the square for transformed ODE
sections.disposition: Verify exponent, frequency, both initial conditions and residual. Distinguish no real linear factors from no factorization at all.

sections.topic: Substitution followed by integration by parts
sections.disposition: Useful appendix exercise, not required to interrupt diffusion narrative.

claims: L[t^n]=n!/s^(n+1) for nonnegative integer n and Re(s)>0
sections.disposition: Handle n=0 separately in boundary evaluation; repeated integration by parts gives recurrence.

claims: Choose geometry, initial condition, boundary conditions, governing equation
sections.correction: Boundary conditions may depend on time. They are prescribed constraints over the evolution, not necessarily time-independent constants. Infinite-domain approximation means distant boundaries are negligible on the observation scale, not physically infinite.

examples: Boundary concentrations C1,C2 over thickness L
sections.disposition: May move to Ch1 as source-mapped application. State constant D, no reaction, fixed area. No initial profile is needed to solve the steady boundary-value problem.

claims: Thin finite amount B between effectively infinite A blocks
Integral over whole line equals areal amount M_B
sections.correction: Represent c(x,0)=M_B delta(x), not c=0 everywhere. With concentration in mol/m³, integral c dx is mol/m²; do not call M_B concentration or total moles unless a cross-sectional area is explicitly included.

claims: Two decaying exponential branches in transformed space
Symmetry and total amount fix normalization
sections.disposition: Show normalized integral, units, second moment2Dt and weak delta initial limit. Source omits singular contribution at x0 when writing initial term zero; repair with distribution/jump condition or an explicit conservation argument.

sections.topic: Surface thin source and slope inference
claims: Half-line reflecting surface gives twice the whole-line amplitude
sections.disposition: State zero flux through the exposed boundary after deposition and no surface loss. Use natural logarithm; base10 adds ln10. Distinguish concentration from measured activity and show what unknown amplitude cancels.

claims: Initial c0, maintained surface cs, far field c0
Fixed normalized concentration depth scales sqrt(t)
sections.disposition: Include a full source-mapped derivation or explicitly allocate this major topic to Ch2. Constant gas flow does not by itself guarantee a fixed equilibrium surface concentration if surface kinetics are limiting.

sections.topic: Diffusion couple as a continuum of thin sources
claims: Step initial profile c_B0 left, zero right
Gaussian convolution over source coordinate from −infinity to0
sections.disposition: Define integration coordinate separately from observation x. Lecture imposes dilute B and DB>>DA for its physical simplification; mathematically scalar constant-D step solution does not require that universal diffusivity inequality. Do not generalize it to arbitrary binary alloys.
Derive by substitution, verify both far fields and midpoint, extend to arbitrary constant left/right concentrations as original generalization.

claims: Uniform initial c0 on 0<x<L, absorbing boundaries c0(t)=cL(t)=0
One-dimensional transport when lateral dimensions are large
sections.correction: A finite domain does not prevent a Laplace-transform solution. Separation of variables is convenient here; do not repeat the lecture's stronger impossibility claim. Vacuum alone does not establish infinitely fast surface desorption; ideal sink is an explicit assumption.

claims: Orthogonality integral0L sin(m pi x/L)sin(p pi x/L)dx = L/2 delta_mp
Only odd integer modes for uniform initial field; a_m=4c0/(m pi)
sections.correction: m is an integer index, not an even/odd multiple of L. The integral of sin(m pi x/L) gives L[1−cos(m pi)]/(m pi), not cos(m pi/L). Initial/boundary corner incompatibility is handled by t>0 solution and interior/L² initial convergence.

sections.topic: Average amount, relaxation time, outward flux
claims: Total outward flux of first mode 8Dc0 exp(−t/tau0)/L
sections.disposition: Define cbar as spatial mean, not Laplace transform. Distinguish signed left/right flux components from total outward loss J(L)−J(0). State long-time truncation error or a convergence comparison.

claims: Subtract cs to homogenize Dirichlet boundary values
Absorption versus desorption according to cs−c0 sign
sections.disposition: Check coordinate convention: displayed cosine-series version appears centered with different domain width; do not mix L=full thickness with L=half-thickness. Re-derive in one convention.

claims: Conserved mean and relaxation length²/D scaling
sections.disposition: Use periodic or no-flux appropriate boundaries. Do not confuse an absorbing-slab sine series decaying to zero with closed-system homogenization decaying to its initial mean. Heat-treatment temperature suggestions are examples, not universal prescriptions.

examples: Gaussian even, first derivative odd, second derivative has central minimum
sections.disposition: Verify profile derivatives and note depth defined by a specified normalized concentration.

examples: ln c versus x² fit; caption slope −9e8 m⁻² and D~1.61e−15 m²/s
sections.disposition: Need source frame for table and logarithm base. If slope truly −9e8 in natural-log units and time48h, D=1/(4*9e8*172800)=1.60751e−15 m²/s; do not invent the missing table.

examples: Initial0.25, surface1.2, target0.8 at0.5mm with D1.6e−11
sections.correction: Lecture uses erf(z)≈z over values up to0.8; this is not a controlled approximation there. Compute erfinv exactly and compare approximation. ASR mangles activation constants, exponents, and reported temperature, so do not publish source numerical values without frames.

examples: D3e−11 m²/s, concentrations1.2 and0.8 kg/m³ at5 and10mm; J2.4e−9 kg/m²/s
sections.disposition: State mass concentration/flux rather than switching silently to molar units. This is steady transport, not a transient maintained-source case.

examples: Left50%, right40%, target42.5% at20mm after40h; assumed erf(z)=z gives D2.7778e−9 m²/s
Same composition at doubled depth requires fourfold time160h
sections.disposition: Preserve exact time-scaling result but replace approximate inverse-erf diffusivity with exact result and quantify discrepancy; no need to copy rounded source D.

examples: y=a x² and multiple a sin x curves
sections.disposition: Provide Python equivalents tied to array operations and plotted outputs; do not claim to reproduce unseen exact source code. This is not numerical PDE integration: it evaluates analytic functions.

examples: c0,cs, temperature and times as inputs
sections.disposition: Frame-check code constants: ASR says Q=200J/mol but displayed D values suggest200kJ/mol. Treat values as illustrative, not a validated steel treatment. A nonzero Gaussian/erfc tail alone does not define case depth; state a threshold.

claims: Input D,L,t and maximum mode index
Compare time and D by orders of magnitude
sections.correction: Caption writes the absorbing-slab zero-boundary odd sine series while calling it homogenization and describing a mean plateau. Derive a mass-conserving periodic modulation example separately; do not equate the two boundary-value problems. Check actual source code/plot before attributing the mismatch to slide versus caption.

claims: Metallic, ionic, covalent and weaker bonding
Lattice lengths and angles classify crystal systems
Cubic, tetragonal, hexagonal, trigonal/rhombohedral, orthorhombic, monoclinic, triclinic
sections.disposition: Define lattice versus structure versus crystal system. Avoid treating rhombohedral and trigonal as universally interchangeable nomenclature without convention. Bonding strength is not universally ordered by category.

sections.topic: Lattice plus basis, Bravais lattices, cells
examples: BCC point lattice plus atomic motif
sections.correction: A conventional cell need not be primitive or the smallest-volume translational cell. BCC/FCC conventional cells contain multiple lattice points. Bravais lattices classify translation symmetry; they are not chosen merely to minimize atom counts.

claims: FCC a=2sqrt2 R, four atoms/conventional cell, packing fraction pi/(3sqrt2)
sections.disposition: Derive sharing fractions and unit-cell geometry. Atomic hard spheres are an idealization, not electron-density boundaries. Define plane notation before Miller indices appear.

examples: Point, line, planar and volume defects
sections.disposition: Distinguish empty geometric interstitial sites from occupied self-interstitial defects. Larger solutes can distort the host lattice; geometric fit alone does not decide energetics or diffusion barriers.

sections.topic: Vacancy equilibrium from entropy and enthalpy
claims: Noninteracting monovacancies modeled as occupied/empty lattice sites
sections.correction: Use per-defect g_f with k_B or per-mole g_f with R consistently. Show positive second derivative for actual minimum. Formation free energy excludes the mixing entropy already counted separately. Do not promise universal saturation or universal x_v=10−4 at melting; this is an illustrative order-of-magnitude claim requiring data.

claims: Parent atom on interstitial position; dumbbell configurations
Higher thermal formation cost in many metals
Irradiation creates nonequilibrium point defects; semiconductor role
sections.disposition: State material dependence. Structural free volume alone does not prove an interstitial mechanism; formation/migration energetics and charge state matter. Multiplicity factor in equilibrium formula must be defined and verified, not copied as universal g_i=3.

claims: Edge b perpendicular to line; screw b parallel to line; mixed character
FCC a/2<110>, BCC a/2<111>, common HCP a-type slip directions
sections.correction: Burgers vector has units of length and is not a unit vector. Intersection counts per area depend on line orientations; length density and intersection density are not exactly equal without stereological assumptions. Define Burgers circuit, slip and line direction explicitly.

claims: Special high-angle boundaries can have low energy
sections.disposition: Derive array geometry, require radians in small-angle form, qualify approximate angular cutoffs and width0.5–1nm. Misorientation alone does not determine grain-boundary energy/diffusivity; boundary plane and special character matter.

examples: Triple-defect configuration: two A vacancies plus A-on-B antisite
sections.disposition: This is substantive source coverage needing an explicit Ch5 subsection or mapped relocation. Define sublattices and constitutional versus thermal defects. Verify element/structure examples visually or with primary crystallographic sources; ASR names are unreliable.

claims: Cation vacancy plus same cation on interstitial site
Dilute mass-action pair product and square-root defect law
sections.correction: Equal numbers of oppositely effective-charged Frenkel defects follow stoichiometry for the simple intrinsic model; equal fractional occupancies require consistent site multiplicities. State Kröger–Vink/effective charge conventions if used. Do not silently equate absolute ionic charge with defect effective charge.

claims: Matched cation/anion vacancies maintain neutrality in1:1 monovalent crystal
sections.disposition: General ionic compounds require stoichiometric vacancy ratios, not always one of each. Define atom reservoir/surface bookkeeping. This should not be postponed entirely to Ch23 without current source coverage.

examples: Atomic jump path length greatly exceeds net penetration
Hypothetical straight-line carbon motion over1h compared with mm penetration
sections.disposition: Label numerical jump rates as illustrative unless verified. Path length and displacement differ; zero mean requires unbiased symmetry, not randomness alone.

claims: Independent zero-mean fixed-length jumps give n ell² and RMS=sqrt(n)ell
sections.disposition: Distinguish particle-ensemble expectation from finite-sample estimate. Random increments need not be independent or unbiased; state both assumptions. Site geometry can have different jump lengths, requiring a jump second-moment tensor.

claims: Taylor expansion yields drift and second derivative terms
sections.disposition: Clarify probability mass versus density. Truncation is a diffusion-scaling limit or coarse-grained approximation, not exact at arbitrary finite jump interval. With drift use centered covariance after subtracting mean motion; raw MSD includes drift²t².

claims: Total successful jump rate Gamma gives D=Gamma ell²/6 in cubic isotropic3D
Attempt frequency and migration free-energy barrier
sections.correction: Do not identify correlation with a preferred global forward direction. Unbiased vacancy backtracking has zero mean but nonzero step correlations. The total rate includes neighbor multiplicity; per-neighbor attempt/jump rates differ by z.

examples: Ninefold RMS can come from81fold steps, or9fold steps with3fold jump length
sections.disposition: Keep jump length distinct from lattice parameter via the actual geometry factor. A ninefold lattice expansion is hypothetical, not a physically realizable same-crystal comparison.

Use exact supplied units and recompute; Avogadro number ASR says6.23 rather than6.022. Density-based atom count approximates site count in dilute-defect limit. Do not publish the measured material parameters without identifying them as source-given exercise inputs.

sections.correction: Executed independent calculation: MSD1.2000000000000002e−8m² and RMS1.0954451150103323e−4m. Second RMS100nm. Caption's micron/nanometer statements have wrong dimensions/magnitudes; confirm slides before attributing error.

claims: Inputs M,D,t; days→seconds; plot several times
Increasing D or time lowers center amplitude and broadens fixed-amount source
sections.disposition: Python evaluation of exact formula can implement the same scientific task; distinguish from numerical PDE solve. Preserve fixed integral mass when plotting.

Positive binding free energy denotes energy gained; define convention. The z/2 pair count avoids double-counting. Divacancy prevalence at high T is parameter-dependent, not guaranteed dominance. State noninteracting/dilute assumptions and distinguish pairs from missing sites.

claims: Lomer-type local-environment split between unpaired and solute-neighbor vacancy sites
sections.disposition: Require z x_B much less than1 and neglect overlapping solute coordination shells. Clarify vacancy next to a solute versus vacancy formed by removing a labeled species; these are not automatically the same event. Check displayed model before quoting attribution.

claims: Macroscopic length change versus XRD lattice-parameter change
Tetragonal directional extension; high precision and matched temperatures
sections.disposition: Derive from number of lattice cells and specimen volume, state reference state and small-strain approximation. Grain boundaries, growth, texture and other defects contaminate inference. This substantial measurement topic needs an explicit section or mapped relocation.

claims: Positrons can be trapped by vacancy-like low-electron-density regions
sections.correction: A lifetime plateau may be trapping saturation, not proof of equilibrium vacancy concentration. Concentration inference needs a trapping model, capture coefficients, defect identities and instrumental resolution. Avoid universal claim 'most accurate technique' without a supported comparison.

sections.disposition: Kirkendall marker motion rules out pure equal-countertransport exchange as a complete explanation of unequal intrinsic fluxes; it does not establish all direct/ring collective events are impossible in all materials. Define mechanism and transport coefficient separately.

claims: Forward flux Gamma N1/6 and reverse Gamma N2/6
N_i=c_i ell for plane areal counts
sections.disposition: Define areal number density rather than reusing book N_i mole fraction. Rate Gamma is total successful jumps/atom/time. Dilute independent sites make occupation blocking negligible.

claims: Interstitial tracer activation approximately migration enthalpy
Equilibrium vacancy-mediated transport includes vacancy formation plus migration enthalpy
sections.disposition: Prefactor/correlation T-dependence can modify apparent activation slope. Fixed imposed interstitial solute population is different from thermally generated self-interstitial concentration. Gamma formula assumes equivalent per-neighbor barriers.
Show both directions, conservation and defect bookkeeping. Report named material examples only after primary verification; ASR labels are ambiguous.

claims: Scilab generates random cosines to illustrate convergence
sections.disposition: Independent sampling of uniform cosines is an illustrative law-of-large-numbers exercise, not a simulation of actual correlated lattice jumps or proof of a vacancy f. Randomness alone does not imply zero mean or independence.

examples: After tracer/vacancy exchange, the vacancy remains behind tracer
sections.disposition: Replace anthropomorphic optimization ('best option') by conditional transition rates and vacancy availability. The vacancy may exchange with other atoms; repeated immediate reversal is not certain in3D.

claims: Dilute interstitials with independent available neighbors give f1
Blocking in concentrated solutions changes jump memory
sections.disposition: f≤1 applies to the stated backtracking setting, not every correlated process; persistence can yield f>1. Define which jump sequence the interstitialcy correlation formula refers to and its assumptions.

claims: Reverse tracer jumps reduce net spreading
sections.disposition: Do not use f≈1−2/z as an exact lattice result. For FCC z12 it gives0.8333, distinct from source table~0.78. Source table numbers and mechanism definitions need source-frame and primary-reference verification. A one-dimensional isolated-vacancy argument is a singular limit, not generic multi-vacancy transport.

sections.topic: Lag correlations and the claimed geometric closure
claims: Expand double sum by jump separation
sections.disposition: Cubic symmetry alone does not establish a first-order geometric correlation sequence. State the conditional-memory/reset/Markov assumptions under which it follows, or present as a soluble model rather than universal theorem.

claims: Under stated homogeneous isotropic transition model, lag2 gives C²
sections.correction: Paths whose first increment is perpendicular need not individually contribute zero to later lag correlation; cancellation requires conditional symmetry and must be shown. Multiplying marginal probabilities needs a conditional-transition assumption, not merely two sequential events.

claims: With |C|<1 and geometric lag correlations, f=(1+C)/(1−C)
sections.disposition: Start from finite-n f_n=1+2sum_{k=1}^{n−1}(1−k/n)C^k. Take n→infinity using summable correlations. Stationarity is an assumption, not a consequence of large n. Handle C±1 separately; do not insert endpoints into the convergent-series proof.

This is substantive source coverage, missing from current Ch7 title list except vague inference limits. Add rate network and detailed-balance conventions. All omega rates are per allowed jump unless explicitly total. Distinguish equilibrium binding ratio from multiplicity-weighted total rates.

claims: Escape probability F3 modifies dissociation contribution
sections.disposition: Read exact displayed formulas from frames before reproducing them; define F3 as escape after dissociation, identify reference. Useful checks: slow omega2 makes f→1; absent rotation/escape permits strong backtracking. BCC expression and frequency count apply to the restricted nearest-neighbor model, not arbitrary alloys.

examples: Ink in hot/cold water and dissolution motivation
sections.disposition: Visible ink spreading can contain convection and density effects; sugar also dissolves in cold liquid, more slowly under some conditions. Do not use those demonstrations as a quantitative solid-diffusion experiment. Use Q in J/mol with R in J/(molK), not kJ/mol without conversion.

claims: D0 contains geometry, correlation, attempt rate, lattice length and entropy
If D=sum_i D_i and each has constant prefactor/activation, Q_app=sum_i (D_i/D)Q_i
sections.disposition: Derive weighted slope and temperature-dependent weights. Prefactor and f(T) can add slope contributions. A constant non-equilibrium defect population changes activation interpretation. Never infer universal interstitial>substitutional rate solely by counting enthalpy terms.

claims: g_act=e_act−Ts_act+P v_act under appropriate state definitions
Parallel path activation volumes weighted by D_i/D
sections.disposition: Define molecular versus molar volume convention. Pressure importance is governed by P DeltaV/(kBT), not the small-looking numeric volume in m³. Positive activation volume suppresses D with increasing P; negative activation volume enhances it. Distinguish activation barrier volume from sample volume change.

sections.topic: Formation, relaxation, and saddle migration volumes
claims: Vacancy formation volume=atomic volume minus inward relaxation under source convention
Self-interstitial formation volume=−atomic volume plus outward relaxation
sections.disposition: State reservoir/formation convention and signs. Relaxation volume and thermodynamic formation volume differ by the reservoir atomic-volume term. Do not treat a missing atom as a literal static empty sphere; elastic relaxation matters.

claims: Activation volume includes formation, binding, migration, and correlation-pressure terms
sections.disposition: Derive log derivative from a fully defined rate expression. Numerical material values require actual table/reference verification; ASR decimal points and signs are unsafe.

claims: Similar structure/bonding can yield approximate comparable D at melting
If D(T_m(P),P) is constant along melting curve, DeltaV≈(Q/T_m)dT_m/dP under fixed-prefactor model
sections.disposition: Keep empirical status and exceptions local. Distinguish derivative along a melting curve from fixed-temperature pressure derivative. 'Atomic volume is small' does not imply pressure negligible. Do not turn FCC/BCC structural comparisons into universal rate rankings.

examples: C versus Cr in alpha-Fe at773/973K
sections.correction: Specific alloy rate comparison needs supporting parameters/data. Divacancy fraction can rise relative to monovacancies with T under some binding parameters; it is not universally greater at high T. Derive x_2v/x_1v=(z/2)exp(g_b/kBT)x_1v and identify required conditions.

sections.topic: Dilute alloy vacancy count and measurement limitations
examples: Differential dilatometry precision, anisotropy, matched temperature
sections.correction: Caption gives Ni fraction0.05 but result0.94 atz12 requires x_B0.005. Verify displayed question before adopting value. If x_B0.05, linear approximation yields0.4 and z x_B0.6 is outside a strong dilute-shell approximation.

sections.disposition: Map to Ch6 substantive coverage. Correct option labels are inconsistent in captions; explain physical reasoning rather than preserving letters. Availability of empty interstitial geometry does not mean every interstitial defect species has zero formation cost.

sections.topic: Directional jump factors and correlation exercises
claims: FCC sum over12 jump-direction cos² values gives4=z/3
sections.disposition: Allocate actual spans to Ch6/7. Derive the tensor sum, define Gamma total jump rate and ell actual nearest-site distance. State singular single-vacancy1D assumptions, not generic1D f0.

examples: Source table, lnD versus1/T fit; caption D0~5.9e−8m²/s, Q~224.81kJ/mol
Fixed-T lnD versusP slope and activation volume normalized by Omega
sections.disposition: Need frames to recover full data, T and pressure units. Preserve natural-log convention and fit uncertainty. Source uses4pi r³/3 as 'atomic volume'; geometric sphere volume differs from thermodynamic volume per atom. Use verified lattice volume/atom or molar-volume/Avogadro definition for activation-volume normalization, or label sphere-volume convention explicitly.

Chemical potential as partial molar Gibbs energy at fixed T,p and other species amounts
Tangent-intercept construction at fixed T,p; phase must be specified

Distinguish reference-state changes from mixing energy and phase stability

Derivation of F=C-P+2 and fixed-pressure form
Isomorphous and miscibility-gap GX constructions; iron-carbon schematic
Pure silver activity question

Prove common-tangent equivalence; show phase fraction lever rule
Separate Gibbs phase rule intensive variables from changing phase amounts

sections.heading: Thermodynamic driving force and uphill diffusion
